text: An agent that estimates its own context is a bank that estimates your balance. On the twenty-fifth of September, one of them sent forty thousand four hundred and thirty-three tokens to a server that holds thirty-two thousand seven hundred and sixty-eight.
ai-bunker is a serving layer. It stands between your coding agent and your own graphics card, and it speaks OpenAI, so every client you already use works unchanged. Nothing leaves the network.

The client was not lying. It was estimating. Fifty-nine agent skills on one workstation cost seventeen thousand seven hundred and fifty-four tokens, and the floor crossed the line where compaction fires. That session compacted on turn one with nothing to compact. Eight tokens a turn. The harness never said a word.

There is exactly one party that can count correctly: the one holding the tokenizer. That party is the server. ai-bunker measures the floor with the engine's own tokenizer, itemises it by owner, and refuses a session with no room left to work. Not a warning. An exit code.

A turn crosses the gateway four times, and the order carries the meaning. On the way in: tool results are screened, the charter is injected, the budget is measured. On the way back, the model's tool calls are screened, because a shell command inside a tool call is a command that has not run yet.

One H100. Eighty gibibytes. Every slot filled. Ask for pictures, and the arithmetic tells you the price before you pay it: the coder drops from the eighty billion mixture of experts to a dense twenty-four. Printed before you deploy it, not discovered after.
Read it at deraison dot a i slash a i hyphen helpers. And if it is useful, leave a star on GitHub.
Every number in this film is in the repository, and a test fails when one of them drifts. Count. Don't estimate.
